newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish shares recover on EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Finnish shares recover on EMU stability pact.

text.p: Firmer bonds and the dollar's gains which followed the EMU stability pact agreed in the weekend helped Finnish shares recover from Friday's losses in fair trade on Monday, brokers said.
The market was also buoyed by Wall Street's stronger opening and the Helsinki general index HEX rose 0.71 percent to close at 2,411.75 points.
"The tone was good and I think we could see more gains on Tuesday," one broker said.
Building materials and cargo handling equipment group Partek closed 1.00 markka up at 70.50 after announcing an extra 2.50 markka dividend.
Trade in the share was boosted by a 111 million markka after-hours deal as Norwegian Aker sold 1.5 million shares to a Finnish insurer-linked company for 74.00 markka per share.
The dollar's strength and a faster forest industry output growth in October helped paper stocks reverse Friday's losses.
UPM-Kymmene advanced 1.30 markka to 94.00, and Enso closed 1.20 markka up at 37.00. Metsa-Serla share rose 1.00 markka or over three percent to 32.70.
Telecoms major and bourse engine Nokia closed moderate trade 0.50 markka higher at 254.50.
